The shift from "learning established knowledge" ( undergrad) to " creating new knowledge" ( grad school) typically intensifies challenges, not reduces them. In many South Asian contexts, where undergraduate education can be highly competitive and exam-driven, graduate programs often require even greater intellectual independence, time management, and expertise in niche areas. While personal experiences vary, the assumption that grad school is "easier" overlooks its inherent complexity and higher expectations. It’s more accurate to say it’s * different*—not simpler.
